tasks.task: I need a quick cross-check for the Steam lists we’ll cite in today’s 09:30 UTC newsletter: confirm the API is healthy enough to use, then pull the most recent (non-expired) Steam Trending and Steam Top Sellers lists and tell me which game is #1 on each. If either list comes back empty, flag it so we don’t publish stale data.

success_criteria: Step 0 returns a health object with status not equal to "down" (it may be "degraded").
Step 1 returns a non-null snapshot and at least 1 item (so we can identify the #1 Steam Trending entry).
Step 2 returns a non-null snapshot and at least 1 item (so we can identify the #1 Steam Top Sellers entry).
The response data from steps 1 and 2 is sufficient to name which game is rank 1 on each list (by title/title_override and/or game_id).

tasks.task: I’m writing today’s (2026-08-03) Steam trends briefing and need the top 5 Steam “Trending” games from the latest ready snapshot (gtm_snp_01J8X4N2WQ8T3P2ZK7H6M1A9VQ). For each, include the canonical game title and store URL from our games catalog, plus the rank and current_players from the snapshot items. This has to be done using only snapshots that are currently ready (not stale/failed).

success_criteria: Step 2 returns up to 5 Steam trending items and includes rank and current_players fields (used for the briefing).
Step 3 returns the catalog record with id gtm_gam_01J8R2N7Q9J7X0R3B2K7T6M4H1 and a non-null store_url for “Baldur's Gate 3”.
Step 4 returns the catalog record with id gtm_gam_01J8R2P1Y1T4W9D7P6V2QZ1C8K and a non-null store_url for “Cyberpunk 2077”.
The workflow uses only ready/valid data by anchoring the fetch to $0.last_successful_snapshot_at (no hard-coded stale/failed snapshot ids).
